newsitem.title: SPAIN: S&P's lowers ratings for Spain's BCH.
newsitem.headline: S&P's lowers ratings for Spain's BCH.

text.p: Ratings agency Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it had lowered its long-term debt ratings for Spain's Banco Central Hispano (BCH) to A- from A, and had cut its short-term ratings to A-2 from A-1.
The bank's long-term outlook was rated "stable", revised up from "negative".
S&P's said the decision was based on BCH's financial profile, which was "weaker than its competitors in the highly competitive Spanish banking market."

Although S&P was confident of the bank's committment to improve asset quality and control costs, "the general costs structure, somewhat oversized, and the necessary effort to improve the quality of its assets mean that a rapid change is more difficult to achieve."
It said the acquisition of 26-36 percent of Banco de Colombia S.A. would represent a "new consumption of capital at a time when the bank's capital is under pressure."

In terms of its outlook, S&P's said BCH has "considerable potential due to the importance of its client base and its branch network," adding that the bank should be able to maintain its market share and stabilise revenues in the future.
